title: Energy-Adaptive Buffering for Efficient, Responsive, and Persistent Batteryless Systems
problem: Current batteryless energy harvesting systems use fixed-size buffers chosen at design time, which waste energy as heat during power surpluses and as leakage during power deficits. Static buffers are poorly suited for volatile environmental power sources.
motivation: Batteryless energy harvesting systems enable new sensing, computation, and communication platforms untethered by power delivery infrastructure or battery maintenance requirements.
method: The system monitors the harvested power coming in and automatically adjusts how much energy it stores. When power input is high, it shrinks the buffer to prevent overflow—energy being wasted as heat when the storage is full. When power input is low, it grows the buffer to prevent underflow—stored energy slowly leaking away unused. By adjusting storage capacity to match the current power level, the system stays able to handle short bursts of work, even as environmental power fluctuates.
key_novelty: The storage buffer automatically resizes based on how much power is available, instead of using a fixed capacity.
contributions: Adaptive buffering mechanism responding to environmental power volatility
Mitigation of energy waste from both overflow heat and underflow leakage
Guaranteed burst operation and improved system responsiveness
Framework for persistent operation in batteryless energy harvesting systems
limitations: Specific implementation details, adaptive mechanism overhead, and detailed comparison with other power-aware approaches not discussed in abstract.
primary_theme: adaptive buffering for batteryless energy harvesting
